sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Years ago, I worked with my friend Julie Shapiro at the Third Coast International Audio Festival.
sentences.zh: 多年前，我曾与好友朱莉·夏皮罗在第三海岸国际音频节共事。

sentences.en: And for more than a decade, Third Coast hosted a competition for short-form documentaries based on a specific challenge.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，第三海岸一直举办一项基于特定挑战的短篇纪录片竞赛。

sentences.en: They were called Short Docs.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为“短篇纪录片”。

sentences.en: We would invite people to make short audio stories inspired by a set of prompts.
sentences.zh: 我们会邀请人们根据一系列提示创作短音频故事。

sentences.en: And we just trusted the fact that if you invite people to make something and give them a little bit of parameters to play with,
sentences.zh: 我们坚信，如果你邀请人们去创作，并给他们一点发挥的空间，

sentences.en: you know, my mantra is like, it always works.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的座右铭是，这总是行得通的。

sentences.en: You can always invite people to get creative and they will always respond in some fashion.
sentences.zh: 你总能邀请人们发挥创意，他们也总会以某种方式做出回应。

sentences.en: Over the years, I must have listened to dozens of short docs and hearing them gave me this jolt of inspiration.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我一定听过几十部短篇纪录片，听它们让我感到一阵灵感的冲击。

sentences.en: They were a reminder about what was possible with audio and how the whole medium benefits when there's a place for all kinds of storytelling.
sentences.zh: 它们提醒着我音频的可能性，以及当有一个容纳各种叙事的地方时，整个媒介会从中受益多少。

sentences.en: However, in recent years, the audio business has changed.
sentences.zh: 然而，近年来，音频行业发生了变化。

sentences.en: Long-form conversation-type podcasts dominate.
sentences.zh: 长篇对话类播客占据了主导地位。

sentences.en: And it's made it harder for documentary and short-form experimental audio to find a home.
sentences.zh: 这使得纪录片和短篇实验音频更难找到立足之地。

sentences.en: Which is why Julie Shapiro and her creative partner, John DeLore, created AudioFlux.
sentences.zh: 这就是朱莉·夏皮罗和她的创意伙伴约翰·德洛尔创建 AudioFlux 的原因。

sentences.en: We thought, you know, everything is longer and longer and longer and longer.
sentences.zh: 我们想，你知道，一切都变得越来越长，越来越长。

sentences.en: So what if we could, you know, create some energy around a short form?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我们能围绕短篇形式创造一些活力会怎样呢？

sentences.en: So John and I decided to create AudioFlux, which is sort of a new version of the Short Docs challenge,
sentences.zh: 所以约翰和我决定创建 AudioFlux，这算是“短篇纪录片”挑战的一个新版本，

sentences.en: but maybe a little bit more for the podcasting age.
sentences.zh: 但可能更适合播客时代。

sentences.en: AudioFlux was recently recognized by The New Yorker as one of the best podcasts of 2025.
sentences.zh: AudioFlux 最近被《纽约客》评为 2025 年最佳播客之一。

sentences.en: And I want to share this project because I'm a big fan of what Julie and John are creating.
sentences.zh: 我想分享这个项目，因为我非常喜欢朱莉和约翰正在创造的东西。

sentences.en: And I want to expand your definition of what a podcast can be.
sentences.zh: 而且我想扩展你对播客定义的认知。

sentences.en: We're going to play some AudioFlux stories in a bit.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿会播放一些 AudioFlux 的故事。

sentences.en: But first, I'm going to talk with Julie about how it all works.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我要和朱莉聊聊它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: So let's start off with a bit of an origin story here.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们先从起源故事开始吧。

sentences.en: How did you and John first arrive at the idea for AudioFlux?
sentences.zh: 你和约翰最初是怎么想到 AudioFlux 这个点子的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so we started in the spring of 2023 talking to each other.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在 2023 年春天开始交流。

sentences.en: John and I had kind of known each other for, known of each other, really.
sentences.zh: 约翰和我其实算是认识，或者说听说过彼此。

sentences.en: We had a lot of people in common because we both had these long histories of working in public radio
sentences.zh: 我们有很多共同的朋友，因为我们都有在公共广播工作的长期经历，

sentences.en: and coming into podcasting, you know, in its early heydays.
sentences.zh: 并在播客发展的早期阶段进入了这个领域。

sentences.en: And so we were talking in the spring because he had just been let go from a job with a big podcast company
sentences.zh: 春天的时候我们聊天，因为他刚被一家大型播客公司解雇，

sentences.en: and I was in between positions.
sentences.zh: 而我当时正处于职业空窗期。

sentences.en: And we were just talking about how morale seemed really low,
sentences.zh: 我们当时就在谈论士气看起来有多低落，

sentences.en: low in the creative audio corner of podcasting and in our community and amongst our friends,
sentences.zh: 在播客的创意音频领域，在我们的社区和朋友中，士气都很低落，

sentences.en: the people we kept talking to felt, I just like really could sense this industry fatigue, you know, at every turn.
sentences.zh: 我们交谈的人都觉得，我真的能感觉到这种行业疲劳，你知道，随处可见。

sentences.en: And we started thinking about what could we do in this moment together that might reverse some of that
sentences.zh: 我们开始思考，在这一刻我们能一起做些什么来扭转这种局面，

sentences.en: or give people something to appreciate, you know, audio for the sake of audio.
sentences.zh: 或者给人们一些东西去欣赏，你知道，为了音频而音频。

sentences.en: And this idea for AudioFlux came out of that kind of motivation to offer something back to the community
sentences.zh: AudioFlux 的想法正是源于这种回馈社区的动力，

sentences.en: and also do something that would bring our own spirits up at the same time.
sentences.zh: 同时也为了做一些能让我们自己振作起来的事情。

sentences.en: So how does it work?
sentences.zh: 那么它是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: Like, how do you get people to do it?
sentences.zh: 比如，你是如何让人们参与进来的？

sentences.en: How do you set up the structure for this sort of challenge?
sentences.zh: 你是如何为这种挑战建立结构的？

sentences.en: So twice a year, we run circuits.
sentences.zh: 我们每年举办两次巡回活动。

sentences.en: And for each circuit, we have a different creative partner,
sentences.zh: 对于每一轮巡回，我们都有不同的创意合作伙伴，

sentences.en: like an illustrator or a pet portrait artist or a writer.
sentences.zh: 比如插画家、宠物肖像画家或作家。

sentences.en: And it's with that partner that the theme for the circuit and the prompts
sentences.zh: 正是与这位合作伙伴一起，我们设计了该轮巡回的主题和提示，

sentences.en: that we invite people to respond to are designed.
sentences.zh: 邀请人们进行回应。

sentences.en: So it boils down to that formula.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底就是这个公式。

sentences.en: And another part of the AudioFlux design is that each story is only three minutes long.
sentences.zh: AudioFlux 设计的另一个部分是，每个故事只有三分钟长。

sentences.en: So why three minutes?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么要定三分钟呢？

sentences.en: So we thought three minutes would be inviting enough to convince people to try,
sentences.zh: 我们认为三分钟足够吸引人，能说服人们去尝试，

sentences.en: to give it a go, to participate in the circuits.
sentences.zh: 去试一试，去参与到巡回中来。

sentences.en: But it's also like this iconic duration, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这也是一个标志性的时长，对吧？

sentences.en: Like three-minute pop songs are very popular.
sentences.zh: 比如三分钟的流行歌曲就很受欢迎。

sentences.en: And these Fluxworks, we call them Fluxworks,
sentences.zh: 这些 Fluxworks，我们称之为 Fluxworks，

sentences.en: almost end up being like songs or like little pop songs that you can listen to over and over.
sentences.zh: 最终几乎就像歌曲或小流行曲一样，你可以反复聆听。

sentences.en: And there certainly are some that I kind of sing along with when I hear them.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些我在听到时会跟着哼唱。

sentences.en: So you can do enough in three minutes to make a really compelling, memorable, profound audio story.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在三分钟内完成足够多的内容，制作出一个非常引人入胜、令人难忘、深刻的音频故事。

sentences.en: But it also is not too daunting if you're trying to do something,
sentences.zh: 但如果你是想做点什么，

sentences.en: you know, in a limited amount of time or for the first time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在有限的时间内或第一次尝试时，它也不会让人感到太畏惧。

sentences.en: I mean, I think most podcast ads are longer than three minutes at this point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得现在大多数播客广告都超过三分钟了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Well, this is our way of protesting against all of the, you know, what's happened to podcasting in a way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是我们抗议播客行业现状的一种方式。

sentences.en: I just, I'm a big, I want, I'm a big podcast fan.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我是一个大粉丝，我想要，我是一个播客大粉丝。

sentences.en: I make podcasts.
sentences.zh: 我制作播客。

sentences.en: I listen to podcasts.
sentences.zh: 我收听播客。

sentences.en: But I have, you know, I think we're all a little frustrated with some of the things that have happened in the industry
sentences.zh: 但我有，你知道，我想我们都对行业中发生的一些事情感到有点沮丧，

sentences.en: and how the kind of imagination has left the building.
sentences.zh: 以及那种想象力是如何消失殆尽的。

sentences.en: So how far along are you with the project?
sentences.zh: 那么这个项目进展到什么程度了？

sentences.en: So we've had two banner years, I must say.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我们度过了两个辉煌的年份。

sentences.en: We have run six different circuits, which means we have partnered with six different creative partners,
sentences.zh: 我们已经举办了六次不同的巡回，这意味着我们与六位不同的创意合作伙伴合作过，

sentences.en: six different sets of rules, six different themes.
sentences.zh: 六套不同的规则，六个不同的主题。

sentences.en: And the life cycle of a circuit is that we commission four pieces from producers who we invite,
sentences.zh: 巡回的生命周期是，我们向受邀的制作人委托制作四部作品，

sentences.en: and then we do an open call.
sentences.zh: 然后我们进行公开征集。

sentences.en: And then anyone can participate in the open call.
sentences.zh: 然后任何人都可以参与公开征集。

sentences.en: And then we pick winners, and we present the winners and the commission works at a big live event somewhere.
sentences.zh: 接着我们选出获胜者，并在某个大型现场活动中展示获胜者和委托作品。

sentences.en: It's really important to us to bring the community together to listen to these pieces.
sentences.zh: 将社区聚集在一起聆听这些作品对我们来说非常重要。

sentences.en: And so we have been always debuting them first in a public setting at a conference or a festival.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直都是先在会议或节日等公共场合首发它们。

sentences.en: And then we put them online, and now we have the podcast for them to appear in as well.
sentences.zh: 然后我们把它们放到网上，现在我们也有了播客来发布它们。

sentences.en: Well, I'm very excited to listen to some of these flux works, as you call them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很兴奋能听到一些你们所说的“Fluxworks”。

sentences.en: So let's start with one from the first circuit of stories.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们从第一轮故事中的一个开始吧。

sentences.en: This one's called The Sound of Silence.
sentences.zh: 这个叫《沉默之声》。

sentences.en: Could you tell us about this piece?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们介绍一下这部作品吗？

sentences.en: So our partner for the first circuit was the incredible artist and illustrator Wendy McNaughton.
sentences.zh: 我们第一轮巡回的合作伙伴是令人难以置信的艺术家和插画家温迪·麦克诺顿。

sentences.en: And with her, we came up with this theme of letting go.
sentences.zh: 和她一起，我们想出了“放手”这个主题。

sentences.en: And this was based on a book that she had written and recently published
sentences.zh: 这是基于她写的一本书，最近刚出版，

sentences.en: after spending some time with people at the end of their lives.
sentences.zh: 是在她陪伴临终之人一段时间后写的。

sentences.en: So the book was called How to Say Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 所以这本书叫《如何说再见》。

sentences.en: And in talking to Wendy, we thought about a theme that wasn't exactly that.
sentences.zh: 在与温迪交谈时，我们想到了一个不完全是那个意思的主题。

sentences.en: But letting go really touched on the things she was drawing and writing about.
sentences.zh: 但“放手”确实触及了她正在绘画和写作的内容。

sentences.en: And so this was the theme we brought to the producers to work with.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们带给制作人们去创作的主题。

sentences.en: And Gregory Warner made this piece called The Sound of Silence, which was about a situation
sentences.zh: 格雷戈里·华纳制作了这部名为《沉默之声》的作品，讲述了他妻子所处的一种情况，

sentences.en: he, his wife, found herself in and, you know, touches on letting go, but also really dives
sentences.zh: 你知道，触及了“放手”，但也真正深入到了他们生活中的特定时间和空间。

sentences.en: into a certain time and place and space in their lives.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们听听吧。

sentences.en: Well, let's hear it.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我妻子萨娜身上发生了这件事。

sentences.en: So a few years ago, this thing happened to my wife, Sana.
sentences.zh: 她会在冥想或读书时听到一种声音。

sentences.en: She'd be meditating or reading a book and she'd hear a sound.
sentences.zh: 一种幽灵般的音调，就在她右耳上方和后方。

sentences.en: A kind of ghostly tone just above and behind her right ear.
sentences.zh: 就好像有人在和我一起读书，并和我一起享受其中。

sentences.en: As though someone were reading over my shoulder with me and delighting in it along with me.
sentences.zh: 在一个快乐稀缺的时代，这是一件奇怪但令人愉快的事情。

sentences.en: An odd but delightful thing at a time when delight was in short supply.
sentences.zh: 大流行的第一个春天，萨娜的精神高度紧张，学校关闭，新闻里充斥着死亡和厄运，

sentences.en: The pandemic's first spring, Sana's mind on high alert, schools closed, death and doom
sentences.zh: 我们俩共用一个狭小的家庭办公室。

sentences.en: on the news, one tiny home office for the two of us.
sentences.zh: 我当时正试图完成工作，而你总是在电话里接受采访。

sentences.en: I was trying to get work done and you were always on the phone in interviews.
sentences.zh: 但那个音调就像一个我可以去的地方。

sentences.en: But the tone was like a place that I could go to.
sentences.zh: 它就像一个我可以进入的圆顶，几乎被静电隔绝了。

sentences.en: It was like a dome I could enter that was almost insulated by static.
sentences.zh: 它让我放下了所有这些高皮质醇的烂事。

sentences.en: It let me let go of all this high cortisol shit.
sentences.zh: 而且这个音调还能让她调频到最日常的时刻。

sentences.en: And the tone could also tune her in to the most everyday moments.
sentences.zh: 我们的孩子在练习钢琴。

sentences.en: Our kid practicing piano.
sentences.zh: 每一个音符都像是一颗投入湖中的鹅卵石，激起了音乐的涟漪。

sentences.en: Every note was almost like a pebble thrown into a lake in such a way that it created these
sentences.zh: 哇，你从来没告诉过我这件事。

sentences.en: musical ripples.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为，你知道，它不是我想象的那样。

sentences.en: Wow, you never told me this.
sentences.zh: 那个音调，不是她想的那样。

sentences.en: Well, because, you know, it wasn't what I thought it was.
sentences.zh: 在你的内耳深处，有这些特殊的毛细胞，纤毛，像海草一样漂浮在液体中。

sentences.en: The tone, not what she thought it was.
sentences.zh: 它们被调谐到不同的频率。

sentences.en: Deep inside your inner ear are these special hair cells, cilia, that float in fluid like
sentences.zh: 如果其中一些小毛发被巨大的噪音或病毒损坏了。

sentences.en: a field of seaweed.
sentences.zh: 现在那个曾经存在的频率或频率范围就不再存在了。

sentences.en: They're tuned to different frequencies.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·亨利博士是耳鸣研究的先驱。

sentences.en: If some of these little hairs are damaged by loud noise or by a virus.
sentences.zh: 大脑在大多数时候处于稳定状态。

sentences.en: Now that frequency or that range of frequencies that used to be there is not there anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以现在它有了这种缺失。

sentences.en: Dr. Jim Henry is a pioneer of research in tinnitus.
sentences.zh: 他说，大脑可以通过……来应对这种听力损失。

sentences.en: And the brain is in a steady state most of the time.
sentences.zh: 过度补偿，通过提高其活动水平。

sentences.en: So now it's got this loss.
sentences.zh: 填补缺失的频率，就像幻肢一样。

sentences.en: The brain, he says, can respond to this loss of hearing by...
sentences.zh: 耳鸣是大脑拒绝放手它曾经拥有的东西的声音。

sentences.en: Overcompensating, by upping its activity.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，我拿到诊断结果时，在回家的路上哭了。

sentences.en: Filling in the missing frequencies, like a phantom limb.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里一直有个念头，就是，是的，你可能正在达到开悟，或者你可能只是在变聋。

sentences.en: Tinnitus is the sound of the brain's refusal to let go of what it once had.
sentences.zh: 我只是选择了相信前者。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I got my diagnosis and I cried on my way home.
sentences.zh: 她现在知道这是一种症状。

sentences.en: I always had in the back of my mind, like, yeah, you could be reaching enlightenment or
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，这些天当她在阅读或专注于美好的事物时……

sentences.en: you could just be going deaf.
sentences.zh: 当文字在你的脑海中变成图像时，音调又回来了。

sentences.en: And I just chose to believe in the former.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，这些音调仍然是她获得某种精神平静的标志。

sentences.en: She knows now it's a symptom.
sentences.zh: 她正在关注当下的一切。

sentences.en: But still, these days when she's reading or concentrating on something beautiful...
sentences.zh: 即使她真正听到的声音只是大脑为失去的东西而唱的悲伤之歌。

sentences.en: When words turn into images in your mind, the tones come back.
sentences.zh: 以上就是格雷戈里·华纳的《沉默之声》。

sentences.en: For her, the tones are still a sign that she's attained some mental quiet.
sentences.zh: 这是一部优美的作品。

sentences.en: She's paying attention to what is here.
sentences.zh: 我特别喜欢它的一点是，我从 NPR 了解格雷戈里·华纳的作品。

sentences.en: Even if the sound that she's actually listening to is just the brain's song of grief for what is gone.
sentences.zh: 他曾长期担任驻外记者，制作过 NPR 的播客《Rough Translation》。

sentences.en: So that was The Sound of Silence by Gregory Warner.
sentences.zh: 这让你看到了他创作能力的另一面。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful piece.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说非常重要，给予……

sentences.en: And what I love about it in particular is I know Gregory Warner's work from NPR.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们想给全新的制作人一个机会去做点什么。

sentences.en: He was a longtime foreign journalist, did Rough Translation, the NPR podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 但也给更有经验的人一个机会去做他们通常不会做的事情。

sentences.en: And this allows you to get a different side of what he can create.
sentences.zh: 我们在格雷戈里身上也感受到了这一点。

sentences.en: That is so important to us to give...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他在各种时长下都是一位大师级的叙事者。

sentences.en: You know, we want to give brand new producers an opportunity to do something.
sentences.zh: 但我们真的觉得他可以用这个作品变得更个人化一点，并将他标志性的 NPR 风格带到这个小小的 Fluxwork 中。

sentences.en: But also to give more experienced people the opportunity to do something else than they usually do.
sentences.zh: 这真是太美了。

sentences.en: And we felt that with Gregory, too.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he is a masterful storyteller at all durations.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们播放下一部作品吧。

sentences.en: And in that film is a scene with Anaya Lockwood, who's this very accomplished field recordist, sound designer, composer, sound experimentaliSt.
sentences.zh: 电影里有一个场景，主角是阿纳亚·洛克伍德（Anaya Lockwood），她是一位非常有成就的现场录音师、声音设计师、作曲家和声音实验家。

sentences.en: And she has this theory of listening with the world instead of listening to the world or at the world.
sentences.zh: 她有一个理论，叫做“与世界共听”，而不是“听世界”或“对着世界听”。

sentences.en: So we grabbed that theme from Sam's film and invited producers to draw from that theme of listening with as they tell a story and also to think about everyday sounds in their environments.
sentences.zh: 所以我们从萨姆的电影中借用了这个主题，并邀请制作人们在讲述故事时，以“共听”为灵感，同时去思考他们周围环境中的日常声音。

sentences.en: And so what's this piece that we're going to listen to from this circuit?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们接下来要听的这期节目里的作品是什么？

sentences.en: Well, this piece is actually it's called In Between Silence by the British producer Talia Augustidis.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这部作品的名字叫《沉默之间》（In Between Silence），由英国制作人塔莉亚·奥古斯蒂迪斯（Talia Augustidis）创作。

sentences.en: And as Talia thought about the story she wanted to tell, she was thinking about the sounds around her versus the sounds that other people are hearing and are maybe forced to hear.
sentences.zh: 当塔莉亚构思她想讲的故事时，她在思考自己周围的声音，与其他人正在听到、甚至可能被迫听到的声音之间的对比。

sentences.en: So at the time, the war in Gaza was in full force, and she wanted to think about the situation for people living in Gaza and their sonic environments.
sentences.zh: 当时，加沙战争正处于全面爆发阶段，她想思考一下生活在加沙的人们的处境，以及他们的声音环境。

sentences.en: And so she sort of took on the role of helping people living in that environment talk about what they were hearing on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 于是，她承担起了一个角色，帮助生活在那种环境中的人们讲述他们每天都在听到什么。

sentences.en: It means an annoying buzzing.
sentences.zh: 意思是恼人的嗡嗡声。

sentences.zh: 这种嗡嗡声已经存在了20多年。

sentences.en: A buzzing which becomes near constant during periods of increased violence.
sentences.zh: 在暴力升级期间，这种嗡嗡声几乎成了常态。

sentences.en: A buzzing which represents surveillance and the looming possibility of a missile strike.
sentences.zh: 这种嗡嗡声代表着监视，以及导弹袭击随时可能降临的威胁。

sentences.en: You try to just get on with things normally, so you try to make food, you try to kind of watch things on TV that will uplift you.
sentences.zh: 你试图让生活恢复正常，所以你尝试做饭，尝试看电视上那些能让你振作起来的节目。

sentences.en: Certain sounds would penetrate that kind of attempt to create normality, and then over time you become habituated to the sound.
sentences.zh: 某些声音会穿透这种试图营造正常生活的努力，久而久之，你就对这种声音习以为常了。

sentences.en: But then the level of anxiety that you're experiencing can then lead to more paranoia about the meaning of the sound.

sentences.en: I think one of the miracles of what audio flux gets to is that there's so many ways to tell stories.
sentences.zh: 我认为Audio Flux（音频流）所达到的奇迹之一，就是讲述故事的方式有如此之多。

sentences.en: I mean, these were two different circuits with two different starting points,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是两个不同的系列，有两个不同的出发点，

sentences.en: but yet they have in common this idea of silence and some manifestation of silence or lack thereof.
sentences.zh: 但它们都有一个共同点，那就是关于沉默的概念，以及沉默的某种表现形式或缺失。

sentences.en: And, you know, one thing you find, and what's really fascinating is how sometimes the fluxworks will talk to each other within a circuit or across circuits.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你会发现一件事，真正令人着迷的是，有时这些Fluxworks作品会在同一个系列内，或者跨系列地进行对话。

sentences.en: And, you know, ultimately, you know, we've had 300 plus fluxworks made across the six circuits.
sentences.zh: 而且，最终，你知道，我们在六个系列中制作了300多部Fluxworks作品。

sentences.en: And it's just, there's such a boundless possibility for storytelling, even in this short duration.
sentences.zh: 这简直是，即使在这么短的时间内，讲故事的可能性也是无限的。

sentences.en: So you take, you know, two producers who have done a lot of other work, each approaching this three-minute challenge or exercise.

sentences.en: And, you know, we learn a lot about Talia through how she tells that story.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们通过塔莉亚讲述故事的方式，了解了很多关于她的信息。

sentences.en: We learn a lot about Gregory through what he reveals about his wife.

sentences.en: But, you know, they're very different in form, different in style, but I think memorable, equally memorable, but just for very different reasons.
